claims.text: Rich Footnotes are a feature that allows users to add context to text, enabling a more immersive writing experience.

supports.quote: Rich Footnotes are a feature that lets Amplenote users imbue **text** with** ****context**[^html1].

claims.text: Rich Footnotes can include various types of content such as images, videos, links, and even previews of other notes.

supports.quote: As you can see by clicking any of these list items, Rich Footnotes can imbue plain text (and by extension, text in Amplenote tasks and calendar events) with all sorts of extra meaning:
- [🖼️  Image](https://images.amplenote.com/0bbee202-0327-11e9-b258-7a639e48bef6/4363d48b-4c60-41c4-ac01-0b3a8816de8a.png)[^html2]
- [📽️  Mp4 video](https://images.amplenote.com/0bbee202-0327-11e9-b258-7a639e48bef6/3dbb2789-129a-491c-b6cb-f01414ed4a81.mp4)[^html3]
- 🔡  Text[^html4]

claims.text: Users can create Rich Footnotes by selecting text and using keyboard shortcuts or toolbar icons on desktop, or by tapping the link icon on mobile.

supports.quote: If you want to insert a **link** (which includes links to Youtube videos, tweets, etc[^html27]), **image, **or **video** into text, just select and paste. Single keystroke -- can't be easier.
If you want to create a Rich Footnote that includes commentary, or if you want to look up a note to link to, open the Rich Footnote dialog. You can do this by highlighting a word or phrase and use
the keyboard shortcut (`Ctrl K` for Windows or `Cmd K` for Mac). Or, you can click the toolbar icons available. On desktop:
*If you're not into using Ctrl-K or Cmd-K, you can click an icon to insert context into your text*

claims.text: Rich Footnotes can enhance writing by allowing writers to include extra details that readers can explore if they are interested.

supports.quote: Which is to say, any given word can diverge from the main topic. This offers extra details to a subset of curious users. Some readers drop with mental energy to dig further into phrases to fully
grasp context. Others are in a hurry and skip the detours, as is their prerogative.
All of which is to say: Heya, curious subset of users! 👋 😊
As an energetic mind, you might be likely to think in multiple directions at once? Such is the audience we hope will try out Rich Footnotes for themselves

calls.question: Why doesn't my task show up next to calendar?

claims.text: You need to set up a Task Domain to see tasks next to the calendar.

supports.quote: calendar](https://www.amplenote.com/help/calendar_visual_guided_walkthrough)[^html1]. Until you've set up a Task Domain, you won't see tasks next to the calendar.
Task Domains are *collections of notes+tags* that Amplenote extracts to-do's from in order to populate the task list [you see next to the

claims.text: The default Task Domains are 'Work,' 'Personal,' and 'Misc,' and they can be renamed or hidden.

supports.quote: The three default Task Domains we offer are "Work," "Personal," and "Misc." As discussed below, any of these Task Domains can be renamed or hidden. The purpose of configuring a Task Domain like
"Work" is to declare the superset of notes and tags that contain tasks relevant to all the projects you aspire to make progress on.

claims.text: Tasks can be drag-and-dropped directly on the Amplenote calendar and synchronized to external calendars.

supports.quote: The tasks you schedule from a Task Domain can be drag-and-dropped directly on the Amplenote calendar and they can be automatically synchronized to one or more external Google or Outlook calendars.

claims.text: If a task is not showing up on the calendar, it might be because it's not included in the Task Domain you're viewing.

supports.quote: Most likely, you are looking at a task that has been scheduled from within a note that is not included in the Task Calendar Domain you're viewing.
[Here is a 3-minute video](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=4cNj7otqr48) and [here is a help page](https://www.amplenote.com/help/using_calendar_task_domains) that explain how to set up Calendar Task
Domains. Basically, you need to pick one or more base tags to be scanned for tasks when looking at a "Work" or "Personal" or custom calendar tab. We do this to prevent stressing users out if they
want to peek at their calendar on the weekend[^html2].

claims.text: You can add a tag to a note to ensure it is included in the Task Domain you're viewing.

supports.quote: Visit your new "Project Tasks" note and add a tag that begins with "`todo`" (the tag that your "Work" Task Domain looks for). For example, `todo/client-projects` or `todo/december-2024`
Use the `!move` task action to move your scheduled task to a different note that has a `todo` tag applied to it (whether it is `todo/projects/recent` or just `todo`, both will work)
Visit your "Task Domain" settings and add either the "Project Tasks" note to your "Work" Task Domain, or add a new root tag to the "Work" Task Domain, that you will apply to the Project Tasks note.

claims.text: You can adjust the Task Domain settings to include specific notes or tags.

supports.quote: Visit your "Task Domain" settings and add either the "Project Tasks" note to your "Work" Task Domain, or add a new root tag to the "Work" Task Domain, that you will apply to the Project Tasks note.
Each Task Domain has several options that control what will show up when you view your Amplenote calendar.
If you don't want all three Task Domains to show from the calendar, you can use this box to hide the task domain.

claims.text: You can customize the color of calendar events based on tags or external calendars.

supports.quote: The simplest set up you can use is to create two tags, one called `work` and one called `personal`, and assign visually distinctive colors to them. Any tasks added to a note part of the `work` tag
(or a subtag of that tag) will be colored in orange, while tasks from the `personal` notes will be light green. Colors - especially contrasting colors - are much easier to spot than text, so your
brain registers that a task is a "personal" task or a "work" task way before it has to actually *read* the task description.
Essentially, adding colors to your Calendar is like a small super power, where you are able to navigate it much faster by getting a quick overview of how your day is split between your main life

claims.text: You can set up a 'Home' or 'Hobby' task domain to hide or de-emphasize certain tasks on the calendar.

supports.quote: If you look at your calendar on Saturday morning, you probably don't want to be reminded of all the upcoming work tasks you have. So, you can set up a "Home" or a "Hobby" task domain, which will
either hide tasks pertaining to work, or de-emphasize the tasks as gray, depending on which options you picked in your settings.

calls.question: How do I have AI write a note for me?

claims.text: To have AI write a note for you, you can use the 'Note Agent' feature within Ample Agent Pro. This allows you to give specific instructions to AI to transform or augment your note.

supports.quote: Want to apply a transformation directly to your note? The "Note Agent" option [added by Ample Agent Pro to Note
Options](https://images.amplenote.com/f8609366-38db-11f1-835b-e59b1941e7c9/6d23b88f-6266-4e2a-a5c3-922f916fcabd.png)[^html1] is ready to augment, transform, or otherwise undertake time-saving work.
*Your wish is Note Agent's command*

claims.text: The 'Note Agent' can perform a variety of tasks such as applying tags, extracting action items, rewriting for clarity, and generating titles for your notes.

supports.quote: Some prompts that we have issued to Note Agent while dogfooding it:
Apply tags to this note based on the existing tag hierarchy
Extract action items / tasks (also possible via the `/suggest` action)
Identify removable words/phrases

claims.text: You can also use the 'Complete that thought' feature, which allows AI to finish a sentence or paragraph you're writing.

supports.quote: Use `/complete` to let AI take a shot at finishing the sentence or paragraph you're writing.

claims.text: For more complex tasks, you can use the 'Task Agent' to let AI work on your tasks by making web searches and referencing related notes within your account.

supports.quote: Why not let AI take a first pass at your todo items?
*Use "/agent" within a task to activate Task Agent*
Task Agent will use any available Rich Footnotes or other context from your todo item, and combine it with your optional input about "what does success look like?" for the task. It will then
